Definition: Start date of the reporting week. Each record represents performance for the week beginning on this date.
Calendar month associated with the reporting period.
Unique identifier for each retail store.
Name of the retail store.
Geographic region in which the store operates.
Sales channel through which the product was sold (e.g., Store, Online, Convenience, Superstore).
Broad product category to which the product belongs (e.g., Dairy, Beverages, Snacks).
Unique code used to identify the product group.
The Product Number (or equivalent product identifier) used to uniquely identify a SKU.
Name of the individual product (SKU).
Customer life stage most associated with the product (e.g., Young Adults, Families, Seniors).
Customer lifestyle segment most associated with the product (e.g., Budget Conscious, Health Focused, Convenience Seekers).
Total sales revenue generated during the equivalent period in the previous year (£).
Total sales revenue generated during the current reporting period (£).
Difference between current sales value and last year's sales value (£).
Percentage change in sales value compared with the same period last year.
Number of units sold during the equivalent period last year.
Number of units sold during the current period.
Percentage change in units sold compared with last year.
Number of customer shopping visits recorded last year.
Number of customer shopping visits recorded during the current period.
Percentage change in customer visits compared with last year.
Number of unique customers purchasing from the category last year.
Number of unique customers purchasing from the category during the current period.
Percentage change in unique customers compared with last year.
Last year average selling price per unit for the company (£). Calculated as Current Sales Value ÷ Current Units.
Current average selling price per unit for the company (£). Calculated as Current Sales Value ÷ Current Units.
Percentage change in average selling price compared with last year.
Percentage of total market sales represented by stores stocking the product. Indicates product availability weighted by store importance.
Percentage change in ACV weighted distribution compared with a previous period.
Percentage of shopping baskets containing the product or category.
Percentage share of customer spending captured by the category relative to total category spending.
Percentage of customers who purchased the product or category more than once within the reporting period.
Number of stores currently stocking and selling the product.
Average sales value generated per store selling the product. Calculated as Current Sales Value ÷ Stores Selling.
Estimated percentage change in sales attributable to price changes.
Estimated percentage change in sales attributable to changes in product assortment or mix.
Competitor's average selling price per unit (£), calculated as Competitor Sales Value ÷ Competitor Units. Used to assess pricing competitiveness.
